statement: A freeze guard that permanently binds the first marker while asking for an operator-reviewed transition has no lawful way to apply a later signed decision. Make supersession an explicit chain over the preceding marker bytes and pin, verify the changing commit with the existing operator-signature reader, and preserve refusal for unsigned edits, deletion, and competing successors. Prove the transition with disposable fixture keys; fixture signatures never authorize the live marker. Controls that already pass on baseline need targeted defence-removal runs: deleting the zero-inventory throw and removing only the __tests__ exclusion must each make its independent control fail. Do not claim every requested control is baseline RED when the original guard already implements that behaviour.

Independent review of the measurement-freeze proposal found that removing the SSH-envelope condition from status === G && ssh broke no test. Real SSH signatures and E/N rejection controls cannot isolate the GPG-versus-SSH boundary: it needs a genuinely trusted OpenPGP signature for which Git reports G, followed by a guard refusal attributable only to the envelope. Every added defence needs a targeted mutation check: remove that predicate in a temporary copy and verify its independent test fails for the expected reason. A green suite is not evidence that each defence is protected against removal.
